messages.author: a4c5d7d1c977b688
messages.subject: details about Nimble samplers
parts:
Dear All,

I have been trying to write my own MCMC in R for a Cormack-Jolly-Seber model with temporally varying survival probability (phi) and capture probability (p). My own algorithm keeps providing biased estimates for some parameters, which I suspect is because I did something wrong in the sampler of z (the true survival status). While my sampler of z (pasted below) is a Gibbs sampler (or at least that's what I believe), the binary sampler in Nimble seems to provide unbiased estimates. Therefore, I wonder if there is a way to dig out the algorithm of this binary sampler of Nimble.

The complete code and some covariates I used for simulating data are also attached. Any help will be greatly appreciated.

Best,
Qing

    # Sample z
    for (v in 1:nindv) {
      if (l[v] <= nyear-2) {
        for (t in (l[v]+1):(nyear-1)) {
          if (z[v,t-1] == 1 & z[v,t+1] == 0) {
            psi_tmp <- phi[t-1] * (1 - p[t-1])
            psi_tmp <- psi_tmp / (psi_tmp + 1)
            z[v,t] <- rbinom(1, 1, psi_tmp)
          }
          if (z[v,t-1] == 0) {
            z[v,t] <- 0
          }
          if (z[v,t+1] == 1) {
            z[v,t] <- 1
          }
        } # t

        if (z[v,nyear-1] == 1) {
          psi_tmp <- phi[nyear-1] * (1 - p[nyear-1])
          psi_tmp <- psi_tmp / (psi_tmp + 1 - phi[nyear-1])
          z[v,nyear] <- rbinom(1, 1, psi_tmp)
        }
        if (z[v,nyear-1] == 0) {
          z[v,nyear] <- 0
        }
      }

      if (l[v] == nyear-1) {
        psi_tmp <- phi[nyear-1] * (1 - p[nyear-1])
        psi_tmp <- psi_tmp / (psi_tmp + 1 - phi[nyear-1])
        z[v,nyear] <- rbinom(1, 1, psi_tmp)
      }
    } # v

messages.subject: Re: details about Nimble samplers
parts:
In addition, if you want to see the sampler in the context of a nimble MCMC object without looking at the full source code, you can do
mcmc$samplerFunctions[[i]]$run
where mcmc is the object returned from buildMCMC and i is the index of the sampler in the samplerList that you want to look at.
You can see the list of samplers (by target node) by
mcmcConf$printSamplers() or mcmcConf$getSamplers()
where mcmcConf is the object returned from configureMCMC.
HTH
Perry

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for pointing me to this valuable information.

This seems to be a Metropolis-Hastings type of sampler such that you pick a candidate value, and then you calculate this acceptance probability to decide if you keep the old value or update it. Is my understanding correct? I do have questions about two lines.

1. Line 129 "model[[target]] <<- 1 - model[[target]]". What is the difference between "<<-" and "<-"? Is the goal of the line to pick the candidate value which is simply the opposite of the current value (because the variable can only be 0 or 1)?
2. Line 134 "otherLogProb <- otherLogProbPrior + model$calculate(calcNodesNoSelf)". It seems currentLogProb is the log probability of the current value (line 128) and otherLogProbPrior is the log probability of the candidate value (line 130; please let me know if I got this entirely wrong), but I'm not sure what calcNodesNoSelf is.

Thank you again for the help!!

Best,
Qing

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: details about Nimble samplers
parts:
It could be viewed as MH but it is really more like a conjugate sampler. There are only two possible values, and the logProb from the current values is stored in (and extracted from) the model. The "other" value is then used, resulting in the information for all possible values and hence a conjugate draw.

"<<-" is R's non-local assignment operator. When assigning from run code to an object (model, in this case) from setup code, nimble requires "<<-" to comply with R when running uncompiled.

The log probability calculations that are needed are split into one for the prior (line 130, where the node being sampled is called "target") and one for the necessary calculation nodes other than target (or "self", so these are the calculation nodes without the target, or calcNodesNoSelf). The reason to do this is if the prior is invalid and hence gives logProb of -Inf, we can avoid doing the other calculations.

You can inspect these objects following my previous suggestion, e.g. mcmc$samplerFunctions[[i]]$calcNodesNoSelf

HTH
Perry
